To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
multirate servers are more efficient than single-rate servers, and predictive service is more efficient than multirate service.

multirate scheduling is a promising technique to exploit the multipexing gains of ATM and that multirate servers with predictive service outperform single-rate servers in terms of the number of sessions that can be admitted.

(a) multirate service is a promising mechanism for transporting VBR video traffic, (b) multirate service outperforms CBR and single-rate servers, (c) predictive service is a viable alternative to multirate service, and (d) measurement-based admission control can further improve the performance of predictive service.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a multirate service for VBR traffic that can be used to improve both the utilization of the network and the delay performance of the applications.
the design of a multirate scheduling mechanism to exploit the multipexing gains of ATM networks, and to provide a flexible and efficient service mechanism to bursty traffic.
the development of a new class of schedulers that are able to exploit the multiplexer gains of ATM networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multirate service is an attractive alternative for VBR video traffic, which is a key component of multimedia traffic.

multirate service is a powerful tool for improving performance and increasing the size of the feasible region in ATM networks, while providing the desired quality of service guarantees to the connections.

the use of a multirate server in conjunction with a measurement-based admission procedure can provide the same level of guarantees as a single-rate server, while allowing more sessions to be multiplexed on a single link.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
multirate service can be used to improve the delay performance of bursty video traffic in ATM networks.
multirate service is a promising mechanism for transporting VBR video in ATM networks.
multirate service is a promising technique to improve the performance of ATM networks in the presence of bursty data traffic, such as VBR video traffic.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the multiplexing benefits of ATM can only be exploited by allowing applications to request a high rate of transmission for brief periods of time, rather than reserving a high rate of bandwidth for the entire session duration.
the multirate service mechanism is a simple and effective way to exploit the multipexing gains of packet-switching networks.
the multiplexing of bursty traffic is a much more complex problem than is generally believed and that the multiplexers need to be designed with the applications in mind.
